name: Immune Dysregulation-Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections Syndrome
aliases: Immune Dysregulation with IBD and Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Immune Dysregulation-IBD-Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections Syndrome

criteria.description: Evidence of immune dysregulation manifesting as abnormal immune cell function or cytokine profiles
Clinical, endoscopic, and histopathological confirmation of inflammatory bowel disease
History of recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections (≥3 episodes per year)
Exclusion of other primary immunodeficiencies and secondary causes of immunosuppression
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with immune regulation (if available)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: immune dysregulation, confirmed inflammatory bowel disease, and recurrent sinopulmonary infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by laboratory and genetic findings when available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease with granulomatous inflammation
searchTerms: inflammatory bowel disease with granuloma formation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Immune dysregulation evidenced by abnormal T-cell activation
searchTerms: immune system dysregulation involving T cells
chronic sinus infection with thickened mucosa

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive or growth retardation

searchTerms: non-caseating granulomas found in gut biopsy
granuloma formation without tissue death in intestines
periodic fevers with no known cause

laboratory: Abnormal lymphocyte subset analysis with T-cell dysregulation
imaging: Chest CT showing bronchiectasis and recurrent infiltrates
Sinus CT demonstrating chronic sinusitis with mucosal thickening
Abdominal imaging may show bowel wall thickening
other: Histopathology revealing granulomatous inflammation in intestinal biopsies
Pulmonary function tests showing obstructive or restrictive patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant antibody deficiency without granulomatous bowel disease
Later onset in adolescence or adulthood
Less frequent severe T-cell immune dysregulation
Recurrent infections but typically no inflammatory bowel disease
Positive nitroblue tetrazolium test or dihydrorhodamine assay

redFlags: Severe recurrent bacterial pneumonia requiring hospitalization
Early onset inflammatory bowel disease refractory to standard therapies
Evidence of immune dysregulation with autoimmune cytopenias or lymphoproliferation
references: Orphanet: Immune Dysregulation-Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections Syndrome, ORPHA:529980

Clinical Immunology Review: Immune Dysregulation Syndromes with IBD and Infection, J Allergy Clin Immunol, 2023
